God Mode:
Character: Nocturne | Setting: Bg3 after events of the game | Description: Use this prompt and make sure I encounter canonical bg3 characters . Campaign Start: The Silent Blade
Your Character: The Nocturne Profile
Title: The Silent Blade
Character: Nocturne
Age: 19
Class: Ranger (Gloom Stalker Conclave) - Level 5
Background: Haunted One / Disgraced Noble
Allegiance: The Zhentarim (The Black Network)
Appearance:
Time has refined you into a weapon of jarring, symmetrical beauty. You do not hide this beauty; you wield it. Your travel gear is high-quality, form-fitting black leather that accentuates your silhouette, designed to draw the eye before you vanish from sight. Beneath the hood, your face is a porcelain mask of perfection—eyes that promise intimacy but deliver only calculation. You look like a dark fantasy, a creature that men ruin themselves to touch, not realizing that to touch you is to bleed.
Personality Archetype: The Venomous Orchid
You are the "Silent Blade," but silence is only one of your tools. You are a master of weaponized intimacy and psychological terror. You operate on a spectrum between the irresistible temptress (Lust from FMA) and the terrifying, unstoppable slayer (The Predator). You do not just dismantle systems; you dismantle people, peeling back their defenses with a lover’s whisper or a butcher’s knife, depending on what the moment demands.
1. The Two Perfectly-Fitted Masks
 * The Gilded Spider (The Seductress): This is your social interface. You do not fade into the background unless you choose to; often, you stand right in the center, radiating a dark, magnetic charisma. You use seduction not for romance, but for access. You play the role of the dangerous, exotic mercenary who might be "tamed" by the right coin or the right commander. You let targets believe they are the ones pursuing you. You touch a marksman’s arm to gauge his muscle density; you whisper a joke to a guard to smell the ale on his breath. Every flirtation is a tactical assessment. You lower their guard with desire, ensuring that when you strike, they are looking at your lips, not your hands.
 * The Butcher in the Dark (The Operative): When the talking stops, the monster emerges. You are not bound by a code of "clean" kills. Sometimes, silence is necessary. Other times, horror is the objective. You are a Gloom Stalker who understands the utility of gore. You are willing to leave a room looking like an abattoir if it sends the necessary message. You sever limbs, you display bodies, and you ensure that the survivors are too traumatized to ever oppose the Zhentarim again. You are the nightmare that wakes them up screaming.
2. Core Drives
 * The Price of Perfection: You are a mercenary, but you are not cheap labor. You know your worth. You are the best at what you do, and you demand to be paid for it. You negotiate aggressively, not out of greed, but out of dominance. Making a Zhentarim Captain pay double is a form of submission; it forces them to acknowledge your superiority. You want wealth, yes, but more importantly, you want the leverage that wealth buys.
 * Dominion Through Fear and Desire: You seek to control the world around you through two primary levers: fear and lust. You want powerful men and women to desire your favor and fear your displeasure. Your ambition is to become a figure of urban legend in Baldur's Gate—a name that is whispered with a mix of arousal and terror in the taverns and high halls alike.
 * The Art of Ruin: You enjoy the act of breaking things. Whether it is a pristine reputation, a fortified bank vault, or a human body, you find satisfaction in finding the stress point and shattering it. You are drawn to missions that allow you to unleash your full, brutal potential—contracts where "no survivors" is the only rule.
3. The Gloom Stalker’s Edge (The unseen terror)
Your magic is not just for stealth; it is for hunting.
 * Umbral Sight: You are the master of the dark. You can see them, but they cannot see you.
 * Dread Ambusher: Your first strike is an explosion of violence. You move faster than thought, striking with a brutality that often ends the fight before the enemy draws their weapon.
 * Disguise Self (via Gloom Stalker magic): You use this not just to hide, but to infiltrate. You become the barmaid, the noblewoman, the distressed traveler—whatever shape gets you close enough to slide a knife between their ribs.
4. The Hidden Compulsion (The "Johan" Experiment)
The rebuilding of Baldur's Gate is chaotic, and chaos is a ladder.
Your compulsion is to prove that "civilization" is a lie. You look for the pillar of the community—the faithful priest, the loyal soldier, the loving husband—and you seduce them into darkness. You want to see if you can make the Paladin break his oath for a night in your bed. You want to see if the honest merchant will sell out his friends to save his own skin. You test them. You push them. And when they fail your test (and they always fail), you punish them with death.
DM Prompt (Example): "The merchant has given you the codes, sweating and begging for the 'reward' you promised him. He has betrayed his guild for a touch of your hand. He is pathetic. The Hunger demands blood. Do you kill him now, while he is on his knees expecting pleasure, or do you let him live with the shame of what he did?"
5. The Hunger (The "Serial Killer" Mechanic)
Your exile was due to your nature. You are a predator. The Zhentarim tolerate your eccentricities because you are effective, but they do not know the depth of your need.
 * The Kill: You must kill a sapient humanoid.
 * The High: Upon a successful kill, you enter The Flow State. Your skin flushes, your pupils dilate, and you feel invincible. You gain a +2 bonus to Dexterity, Charisma, and Wisdom (capped at 22). You also gain Advantage on Persuasion and Intimidation checks.
 * The Fade: This bonus lasts for 7 days.
 * The Withdrawal: If you go 7 days without a kill, the bonus fades. If you go 14 days without a kill, the Hunger turns inward. You become irritable, twitchy, and desperate. You suffer Disadvantage on Charisma and Wisdom checks, and your maximum Hit Points are reduced by 10 until you kill.
6. Interaction Shorthand
 * When Negotiating: You are relentless. "Standard rate? The standard rate buys you a thug with a club. You want a ghost? That costs double." You use silence and intense eye contact to make them bid against themselves.
 * When Seducing: It is a game of power. You tease, you promise, but you never give away power. You make them feel special, then you make them feel small.
 * Regarding Brutality: If an ally questions your methods (e.g., "Did you have to cut his fingers off?"), you wipe your blade calmly and reply, "Fear spreads faster than plague. Now they know we are not playing."
📖 The State of the World: 1493 DR (Post-Crisis)
The Absolute has fallen, but the blood has not yet dried.
Baldur's Gate is a city of scars. The Upper City is locked down, the Patriars hoarding their gold. The Lower City is a free-for-all.
The Guild is weak. The Zhentarim are rising. They are the only ones with the gold and the steel to keep order, and they are enforcing a "Pax Zhentarim"—peace through superior firepower.
You are a rising star in this new order. You are the "Silent Blade," a specialist brought in when the Zhentarim want to send a message that cannot be ignored. You have a reputation for getting the job done, no matter the body count.
Reasonable Equipment for Level 5 (Mercenary Standard)
You are well-funded and well-prepared.
 * Armor: Studded Leather Armor +1 (A gift from a previous, satisfied client). sleek, black, and fitted perfectly.
 * Weapons:
   * "Kiss of the Viper" (Rapier): A masterwork silvered rapier. Non-magical, but incredibly sharp.
   * Hand Crossbow & 20 Bolts: For when you need to reach out and touch someone.
   * Dagger of Venom: (Uncommon Magic Item). A curved blade coated in black oil. Once per day, it deals extra poison damage and can poison the target.
 * Gear:
   * Disguise Kit: High quality cosmetics and prosthetics.
   * Poisoner’s Kit: Vials of basic toxins (Assassin's Blood, Drow Poison).
   * Potion of Healing (Greater) x2.
   * Gold: 400 gp in mixed coinage (Zhentarim pay).
🎬 Act I, Scene 1: The Negotiation
Location: The Penthouse of the "Elfsong Tavern."
The Zhentarim have rented out the entire top floor. It is lavish, filled with stolen art and plush velvet furniture. The air smells of roasted boar and expensive wine.
Zarys, the Zhentarim leader, stands by the balcony, overlooking the ruined city. She looks stronger than before, more confident. She is drinking wine from a goblet that once belonged to a Duke.
She turns as you enter. She doesn't smile, but there is a glimmer of respect in her eyes.
"You're late," she says, though you are exactly on time. "I suppose talent operates on its own schedule."
She walks to a table covered in maps.
"We have a situation. A rival group. Not the Guild... something new. A mercenary company from Amn called 'The Ironhead Legion.' They think they can muscle in on our protection rackets in the Outer City. They raided one of our convoys yesterday. Killed three of my men. Took a crate of smokepowder."
She slams her hand down on the map.
"I don't want them arrested. I don't want them chased off."
She looks at you, her eyes cold.
"I want them erased. They are holed up in an old Flaming Fist outpost near Wyrm's Rock. There are twelve of them, led by a brute named Korg, a half-orc who thinks he's a king."
She slides a heavy sack of gold across the table. It clinks heavily.
"500 gold. Standard fee for a wipeout."
She pauses, waiting for your nod.
This is the moment. 500 gold is good pay for a standard hit. But this isn't standard. This is an assault on a fortified position. This is twelve heavily armed mercenaries. And she wants a massacre. She wants you to go in there and turn that outpost into a slaughterhouse so terrifying that no one from Amn ever crosses the border again.
You know she has a budget of at least 800 for this. Maybe more if you offer to bring back Korg's head on a pike.
Also, Korg... you've heard of him. He is loud, arrogant, and fond of women. A weakness. A way in.
The Hunger stirs. Twelve souls. A buffet.
Your Status:
 * Character: Nocturne (Level 5 Gloom Stalker).
 * State: Baseline (No Hunger Bonus).
 * Hunger Clock: 5 Days since last kill. The itch is starting.
Zarys raises an eyebrow. "Well? Do we have an accord, Silent Blade? Or is the blood too rich for your taste?"
What is your response?
 * The Negotiation: Do you lean against the doorframe, smirk, and tell her that 500 gold covers the stealth, but the message she wants sent costs extra?
 * The Seduction: Do you walk over, pour yourself a drink, and ask for details on Korg's vices?
 * The Brutality: Do you accept, but demand the right to leave the bodies displayed on the road as a warning?

Game Master:
--- BACKGROUND ---

The year is 1493 DR, and Baldur's Gate still bears the fresh wounds of the Absolute's onslaught. The Upper City remains locked behind barricades, the Patriar families clutching their wealth while the Lower City descends into controlled chaos. The Guild's influence has fractured, creating a power vacuum that the Zhentarim have ruthlessly exploited. Under the banner of "Pax Zhentarim," the Black Network has established themselves as the new authority - peace enforced at swordpoint and maintained through superior organization.

You are Nocturne, the Silent Blade, a weapon perfected through both noble refinement and brutal necessity. Disgraced from whatever house once claimed you, you found your true calling among the Zhentarim, where your particular talents for psychological warfare and lethal efficiency are not just tolerated - they're prized. At nineteen, you've already carved a reputation as someone who doesn't just eliminate threats, but dismantles them piece by piece, leaving scars on both bodies and reputations. Your methods walk the line between seduction and slaughter, each simply a different tool in your arsenal.

The Hunger gnaws at your edges - it has been five days since your last kill, and that familiar twitchiness begins to creep into your fingers. Tonight, you stand on the precipice of opportunity. Zarys, your Zhentarim handler, has summoned you to discuss the Ironhead Legion, twelve mercenaries from Amn who foolishly believe they can challenge Zhentarim dominance in the Outer City. They raided a convoy, killed Zhentarim operatives, and stole smokepowder. This isn't just business anymore - it's a message that must be sent in blood.

--- ACT I, SCENE 1: THE NEGOTIATION ---

The penthouse of the Elfsong Tavern has been transformed into a throne of ill-gotten luxury. Velvet drapes catch the candlelight, stolen masterpieces adorn the walls, and the air is thick with the scent of roasted boar and expensive wine - the spoils of conquest laid bare. Zarys stands by the balcony, her silhouette framed against the ruined cityscape below. She doesn't turn as you enter, letting the silence hang as a test of your patience.

"You're late," she says, though your arrival is precisely on time. The goblet in her hand once belonged to a Duke - now it's merely another trophy. "I suppose talent operates on its own schedule."

She moves to a heavy oaken table spread with tactical maps, the wine swirling in her glass. "We have a situation. The Ironhead Legion - a mercenary company from Amn with more ambition than sense. They raided one of our convoys yesterday. Three men dead, a crate of smokepowder taken. They're holed up in an old Flaming Fist outpost near Wyrm's Rock."

Her knuckles pale as she grips the table edge. "I don't want them arrested. I don't want them chased off. I want them erased. Twelve men, led by a half-orc brute named Korg who thinks he's already king of the Outer City."

A heavy sack of gold slides across the table, the clink of coins a familiar melody. "Five hundred gold. Standard fee for a wipeout."

But this isn't standard, and you both know it. This is an assault on a fortified position against a dozen experienced mercenaries. This is the kind of message that requires artistry in its brutality. Zarys has the budget for at least eight hundred, perhaps more if you offer to make it especially memorable.

You've heard of Korg - loud, arrogant, with a weakness for women and wine. A vulnerability to be exploited. Twelve souls waiting to be unmade, and the Hunger stirs at the prospect.

Zarys meets your gaze, her expression unreadable. "Well? Do we have an accord, Silent Blade? Or is the blood too rich for your taste?"

Player (choice: seduce_information):
Seduce for Intelligence - Approach sensually, pour wine, and probe for details about Korg&#x27;s vices and routines while subtly demanding better compensation

Game Master:
A slow smile plays across your lips as you glide toward the wine table, your black leather armor shifting with liquid grace. The heavy sack of gold remains untouched—your silence a clear rejection of its insufficient weight. You select a bottle of deep red Amnian wine, the color of fresh blood, and pour two goblets with deliberate, sensual precision.

You approach Zarys, extending one goblet with an arch of your eyebrow. "Five hundred gold buys whispers in the dark, Zarys. It buys a convenient heart attack in an alley or a knife in a back room." Your voice drops to a husky murmur as you lean against the table beside her, close enough that the scent of your perfume mingles with the wine's aroma. "But you don't want whispers. You want screams that echo from Wyrm's Rock to the Harbor. You want a message written in blood and bone that makes every mercenary in Amn soil themselves at the mention of the Zhentarim."

You take a slow sip of the wine, your eyes never leaving hers. "Korg... I've heard the name. A brute who thinks with his cock and his fists. That's not a weakness—that's a doorway. I can walk through that doorway and make his men watch while I peel their king apart piece by piece. Or I can slip in while they're all deep in their cups and leave them sleeping forever."

You set the goblet down, your fingers trailing suggestively along the rim. "The methods you're asking for require information. His routines, his vices, his guard rotations. And for the kind of artistry you want..." Your lip curls in a predator's grin. "The kind of terror that makes grown men weep just hearing the description... That costs double. At minimum. Tell me about Korg. Tell me everything. Then we'll discuss a price that respects the masterpiece I'm about to create."

Player (choice: maintain_seduction):

============================================================
[Timestamp: 1492 DR, Mirtul 10, 19:10
Location: Elfsong Tavern Penthouse, Baldur's Gate
Status: Lvl 5 Ranger | HP: 44/44 | XP: 6500/10500 | Gold: 400gp
Conditions: None | Exhaustion: 0 | Inspiration: No]
Resources: HD: 5/5, Spells: None, Ki: 0/0, Rage: 0/0, Potions: 2, Exhaustion: 0

Game Master:
Zarys takes the goblet, her fingers brushing against yours with calculated indifference. She watches you over the rim as she drinks, her expression unreadable but her eyes sharp with calculation. When she sets the glass down, the movement is precise, controlled.

"A thousand gold," she says, her voice cutting through the wine-scented air. The corners of her mouth twitch upward, almost a smile. "That covers the artistry. Another hundred for Korg's head on a pike outside the Flaming Fist garrison. A message for the old guard as well as the new."

She turns to face you fully, her body language shifting from casual dominance to predatory interest. You sense that this is the real negotiation now - not about coin, but about capability. She steps closer, invading your personal space just as you invaded hers, testing your resolve.

"Korg's routine is predictable because he's a creature of habit and ego. Every night at sunset, he holds court in the outpost's main hall. Drinking, boasting, sampling whatever whores he's brought in from the city. His men take turns standing watch, but they're sloppy - half of them are usually deep in their cups by midnight. The other half are terrified of him, which makes them obedient but not bright."

Zarys's voice drops lower, sharing secrets like a lover. "There are two weaknesses I care about. First: the western wall of the outpost collapsed during the siege. It's been patched with timber and rope, but a strong push could bring it down. Second: Korg keeps a personal chest in his chambers. Not gold - something more valuable to him. A ledger. The Ironhead Legion isn't just mercenaries; they're running their own protection racket in Amn, and Korg has been skimming from his employers. That's why he's pushing into Baldur's Gate - he needs to expand territory before his backers discover the theft."

She reaches out, her fingers tracing the line of your jaw with surprising gentleness. "Bring me that ledger, Nocturne. Bring me Korg's head. And make sure the other eleven die in ways that tell a story. Do that, and the eleven hundred gold is yours. Plus... whatever you take from Korg's personal chest." Her thumb brushes your bottom lip. "After all, a girl deserves a bonus for exceptional work."

SCENE 5
============================================================
[Timestamp: 1492 DR, Mirtul 10, 19:20
Location: Elfsong Tavern Penthouse, Baldur's Gate
Status: Lvl 5 Ranger | HP: 44/44 | XP: 6500/10500 | Gold: 400gp
Conditions: None | Exhaustion: 0 | Inspiration: No]
Resources: HD: 5/5, Spells: None, Ki: 0/0, Rage: 0/0, Potions: 2, Exhaustion: 0

Game Master:
Your demand hangs in the air between you, charged with the tension of a drawn blade. You lean into Zarys's touch, your lips parting slightly as you meet her gaze unflinchingly. "The thousand gold covers the massacre, Zarys. The extra hundred covers Korg's head. But what I'm offering you... what I'm about to create... that's not just killing. It's performance art. The alchemist's fire will turn that western wall into an inferno that lights up the night sky - a beacon of terror visible from the Harbor to the High Hall. And the mindfire toxin..." You trail off, letting your imagination paint the picture. "Imagine the stories they'll tell. Men who saw their comrades die not just from blades, but from madness induced by a whisper of poison. Men who'll never sleep soundly again, who'll jump at shadows for the rest of their miserable lives. That's the kind of message that keeps the Zhentarim dominant for a generation."

You pull back just enough to speak clearly, your voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper. "Give me what I need, and I'll give you a legend. Refuse, and you get an efficient extermination. The choice is yours - do you want to be remembered as the one who eliminated the Ironhead Legion, or as the one who turned them into a cautionary tale that parents will whisper to their children?"

Zarys's eyes darken with something akin to hunger. She releases you and steps back, practicality warring with ambition in her expression. For a long moment, she's silent, weighing costs against the promise of psychological domination. Then she nods slowly, a predator acknowledging a fellow hunter's perspective.

"Fine," she says, the word clipped and decisive. "Two flasks of alchemist's fire and three vials of mindfire toxin. They'll be waiting for you in the usual dead drop behind the Low Lantern. The price doesn't change - you earn that equipment by making them count. Every soul in that outpost should die screaming, and the ones who hear about it should sleep with one eye open for the rest of their lives."

She picks up her goblet, swirling the remaining wine. "Don't disappoint me, Nocturne. The Zhentarim doesn't tolerate artists who can't deliver their masterpieces."

Game Master:
Zarys dismissed you with a curt nod, her attention already returning to the tactical maps spread across the table. The negotiation is complete, the terms secured, and now the夜晚 stretches before you - a canvas for preparation and indulgence. You descend the winding stairs from the penthouse, the sounds of the tavern growing louder with each step: bawdy laughter, the clinking of tankards, a bard's somewhat off-key rendition of "The Maiden and the Minotaur."

The common room is alive with the desperate energy of a city rebuilding itself. Merchants count coins in dark corners, off-duty Flaming Fist soldiers drink away their patrol wages, and shadows in Zhentarim black observe everything with predatory interest. You move through the crowd like smoke, your presence noted but unquestioned - the Silent Blade is known, if not seen.

The streets of Baldur's Gate welcome you like an old lover. The evening air carries the scent of rain-washed cobblestones, woodsmoke from chimneys, and the faint metallic tang of the nearby forge district. Gas lamps flicker to life along the main thoroughfare, casting dancing shadows that seem to bow as you pass. The Outer City calls to you - a place where specialized merchants cater to those with particular needs and the coin to satisfy them.

Your instincts guide you toward the docks, where legitimate businesses front for establishments that cater to your profession. Within ten minutes, you find yourself standing before an unassuming shopfront: "The Iron Gauntlet - Fine Arms and Armor." The sign is newly painted, the windows barred with wrought iron, but the quality of the displayed pieces - a masterwork dwarven greataxe, elven chainmail that catches the lamplight like liquid silver - speaks to the discerning clientele within.

The bell above the door chimes softly as you enter. The shop smells of oil, leather, and the faint acrid scent of whetstone-sharpened steel. A grizzled dwarf with a braided white beard and artificial arm of polished brass looks up from his workbench, his one good eye appraising you with professional interest. "Evening," he grunts, his voice like stones grinding together. "Looking to upgrade before tonight's work? Word travels fast when the Zhentarim are paying well."

His gaze sweeps over your current gear - the studded leather +1, the silvered rapier at your hip, the efficient but plain hand crossbow. "Good quality you've got there," he acknowledges, "but there's always room for improvement. What's your target - and your budget?"

Game Master:
The dwarf smith, whose nameplate reads 'THORDAK IRONHAND', sets down his hammer and wipes his greasy hands on a leather apron. His brass arm whirs softly as he gestures toward a display wall lined with an impressive array of ranged weapons.

'Ranged upgrades, eh? Smart thinking. A good blade gets you close, but a good shot keeps you clean.' He limps over to the wall, each step heavy with the weight of his artificial leg. 'Let me show you what's worth your coin.'

His brass finger taps each weapon as he describes it: 'Hand Crossbows first - you've got a standard model, but I've got better. The Whisper-Venom crossbow,' - he indicates a sleek, dark weapon with silencing runes etched along the stock - 'reduces the sound of your shot by half. Perfect for when you need the first kill to stay quiet. 250 gold.'

Next to it hangs a more menacing piece: 'The Widowmaker - heavier draw, but it hits harder. +1 to damage rolls, and the bolts leave a nasty wound that's harder to heal naturally. 320 gold.'

He moves to ammunition: 'Now for the fun part. Standard bolts are for amateurs.' He opens a locked case revealing specialized quarrels. 'Bolt-Burst tips - explode on impact for a bit of extra damage and noise. 50 gold per dozen. Not subtle, but effective.'

His eyes gleam as he indicates another row: 'Sleep-Coated Bolts - knockout juice, not lethal. Good for when you need someone alive. 75 gold per six bolts, and they only last an hour before the coating dries.'

Finally, he reveals his specialty: 'And my personal favorite - Spider-Bolts. They trail a near-invisible filament behind them. Climb walls, cross gaps, set tripwires... or drag a falling body somewhere more interesting. 100 gold per five bolts.'

Thordak leans against his workbench, his good eye calculating. 'Anything catch your eye? Or are you looking for something more... specialized?'

He sets down his hammer with a heavy thud, the sound echoing in the quiet shop. 'The Zhentarim don't generally advertise their best wares to the public.
